prompt.zh-TW: 速達機車行這一期虧損 {{money:vars.loss}}，帳上的現金卻比期初多了 {{money:vars.inc}}。哪一個說法最合理？
prompt.en: Swift Scooter Repairs made a loss of {{money:vars.loss}} this period, yet its cash is {{money:vars.inc}} higher than at the start. Which explanation is most reasonable?

text.zh-TW: 現金可能來自借款、出資或收回舊帳，和這一期的利益無關
text.en: The cash may have come from loans, capital or old receivables, all unrelated to this period’s profit

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。錢的來源很多種，只有其中一部分和這一期的利益有關。
feedback.en: Nice work. Cash has many sources, and only some of them have anything to do with this period’s profit.

short.zh-TW: 現金來自借款、出資或收回舊帳
short.en: Cash from loans, capital or old receivables

text.zh-TW: 不可能：虧損代表錢賠掉了，現金一定比期初少
text.en: Impossible; a loss means money was lost, so cash must be lower than at the start

feedback.zh-TW: 虧損的公司常常現金吃緊，這個印象沒錯。不過虧損說的是「這一期的收入少於費用」，現金的增減還要看籌資與投資活動，以及應收、應付的變化；兩者可以反向。
feedback.en: Loss-making companies are often short of cash, and that impression is fair. But a loss only says that this period’s revenue fell short of its expenses; the change in cash also depends on financing and investing activities and on receivables and payables, so the two can move in opposite directions.

text.zh-TW: 虧損的金額可能算錯了，現金增加就表示其實有賺錢
text.en: The loss may be a mistake; more cash means the company actually made a profit

feedback.zh-TW: 你把現金當成檢查利益的方法，這個想法可以理解。不過現金變多可以完全來自借款或股東出資；要檢查利益對不對，該看的是損益表上的收入和費用。
feedback.en: Using cash as a check on profit is an understandable idea. But a rise in cash can come entirely from a loan or from shareholders; to check the profit figure, look at the revenue and expenses on the income statement.

short.en: The loss may be a mistake

explanation.zh-TW: {{term:tm_n4e8t2jy}}和現金的增減是兩個不同的問題。借款與出資（屬於{{term:tm_f9a4c6md}}）、收回舊帳款，都會讓現金變多而不影響這一期的利益，所以答案是{{option:o_0kta}}。{{option:o_bf6n}}與{{option:o_n36q}}都假設兩者一定同方向。
explanation.en: {{term:tm_n4e8t2jy}} and the change in cash are two different questions. Loans and capital under {{term:tm_f9a4c6md}}, and collecting old receivables, all raise cash without touching this period’s profit, so the answer is {{option:o_0kta}}. {{option:o_bf6n}} and {{option:o_n36q}} both assume the two must move together.
